title: GlusterFS: Sync FOP procedure enum with current GlusterFS
description:
## What

Sync the GlusterFS dissector's FOP procedure enum with current GlusterFS, fixing the mislabeling and
non-decoding of all FOP procedures with number ≥ 41.

Closes #21359.

## Why

The dissector's `gf_fop_procnum` enum (`epan/dissectors/packet-gluster.h`) carried a phantom
`GFS3_OP_FORGET` between `READDIRP` and `RELEASE`. `FORGET` is an internal GlusterFS fop that is never
sent over RPC and is absent from GlusterFS's wire enum (`rpc/rpc-lib/src/protocol-common.h`). The
extra entry shifted every procedure constant from `RELEASE` (41) onward by one, so on current
GlusterFS (4.x+) the dissector mislabeled `RELEASEDIR` as `RELEASE`, `FALLOCATE` as `FREMOVEXATTR`,
etc., and left `RELEASE` and `SEEK` unnamed. The enum also stopped at `SEEK`, and
`glusterfs4_0_fop_proc[]` lacked an `IPC` entry, so ops added since (COMPOUND…COPY_FILE_RANGE) were
undecoded. Same RELEASE/RELEASEDIR class as #12614, regressed as GlusterFS added FOPs over time.

## What changed

- `epan/dissectors/packet-gluster.h` — remove `GFS3_OP_FORGET`; append `COMPOUND, LEASE, GETACTIVELK,
  SETACTIVELK, ICREATE, NAMELINK, PUT, COPY_FILE_RANGE` before `GFS3_OP_MAXVALUE`.
- `epan/dissectors/packet-glusterfs.c` — add `IPC` plus those ops to `glusterfs4_0_fop_proc[]`
  (→ `dissect_rpc_unknown`); drop `FORGET` and append the ops to the `glusterfs3_1_fop_proc_vals[]`
  value_string.

Payload dissection for the newly-named ops is left as `dissect_rpc_unknown` — this is a naming-only
fix; field-level decoders for IPC/LEASE/etc. are a separate enhancement.

## Verification

Verified against the GlusterFS 11.2 capture attached to #21359. Built tshark from this branch and
re-decoded: procedures 41/42/44/48 now decode as `RELEASE` / `RELEASEDIR` / `FALLOCATE` / `SEEK`
(previously `proc-41` / `RELEASE` / `FREMOVEXATTR` / `proc-48`). The procedure numbering was
cross-checked against GlusterFS `rpc/rpc-lib/src/protocol-common.h` (`enum gf_fop_procnum`).

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude, via Claude Code); all steps human-verified.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -350,7 +350,6 @@ enum gf_fop_procnum {
 	GFS3_OP_SETATTR,
 	GFS3_OP_FSETATTR,
 	GFS3_OP_READDIRP,
-	GFS3_OP_FORGET,
 	GFS3_OP_RELEASE,
 	GFS3_OP_RELEASEDIR,
 	GFS3_OP_FREMOVEXATTR,
@@ -359,6 +358,14 @@ enum gf_fop_procnum {
 	GFS3_OP_ZEROFILL,
 	GFS3_OP_IPC,
 	GFS3_OP_SEEK,
+	GFS3_OP_COMPOUND,
+	GFS3_OP_LEASE,
+	GFS3_OP_GETACTIVELK,
+	GFS3_OP_SETACTIVELK,
+	GFS3_OP_ICREATE,
+	GFS3_OP_NAMELINK,
+	GFS3_OP_PUT,
+	GFS3_OP_COPY_FILE_RANGE,
 	GFS3_OP_MAXVALUE
 };

commits_data.message:
GlusterFS: Sync FOP procedure enum with current GlusterFS

The dissector's gf_fop_procnum enum (epan/dissectors/packet-gluster.h)
included a phantom GFS3_OP_FORGET between READDIRP and RELEASE. FORGET
is an internal GlusterFS fop that is never sent over RPC and is absent
from GlusterFS's wire enum (rpc/rpc-lib/src/protocol-common.h). The
extra entry shifted every procedure constant from RELEASE (41) onward
by one, so against current GlusterFS (4.x and later) the dissector
mislabeled RELEASEDIR as RELEASE, FALLOCATE as FREMOVEXATTR, and so on,
and left RELEASE and SEEK unnamed.

The enum also stopped at SEEK, and glusterfs4_0_fop_proc[] lacked
entries for IPC and the FOPs added since, so procedures 49 and up
rendered as "proc-N".

Remove the phantom FORGET; extend the enum and the
glusterfs3_1_fop_proc_vals[] value_string with COMPOUND, LEASE,
GETACTIVELK, SETACTIVELK, ICREATE, NAMELINK, PUT and COPY_FILE_RANGE;
and add IPC plus those ops to glusterfs4_0_fop_proc[]. Payload
dissection for the added ops uses dissect_rpc_unknown; this change
corrects procedure naming only.

Verified against a GlusterFS 11.2 capture: procedures 41/42/44/48 now
decode as RELEASE / RELEASEDIR / FALLOCATE / SEEK (previously proc-41 /
RELEASE / FREMOVEXATTR / proc-48).

Same RELEASE/RELEASEDIR class as #12614, which regressed as GlusterFS
added FOPs over time.
